title: incident snapshot stream and cross-team escalation hooks
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: incidents often start with sparse signals and responders spend minutes assembling context. This change introduces a lightweight streaming snapshot mechanism that begins capturing prioritized diagnostics the moment an incident is created, plus configurable cross-team escalation hooks that post a privacy-scrubbed incident brief and actionable suggestions to downstream channels (Slack, PagerDuty, email). Design summary: 1) Snapshot Streamer - starts on incident creation and continuously collects: recent logs (tail with size cap), top traces (trace IDs), metric deltas, active KV cache summary, and a short TTLed heap-profile sample for JVM/Go processes where available. The streamer uses a ring buffer to keep memory predictable and exposes an on-demand export API. 2) Escalation Hooks - pluggable adapters that can enrich a short incident brief with runbook snippets, safe-rollback suggestions (based on deployment metadata), and a curated set of links (dashboard, traces, recent deploys). Hooks run with rate limits and support per-team allowlists/denylists. 3) Privacy & sanitization - built-in scrubbing rules for tokens, emails, PII patterns, and an opt-out policy for teams handling regulated data. 4) Runbook templating - a new template renderer that fills common diagnostic placeholders (last_deploy, error_rate_pct, offending_service) and attaches quick commands for responders. Checklist: [x] Snapshot streamer implementation with ring buffer and exporter, [x] Escalation hook adapter framework, [x] Slack and PagerDuty adapters, [x] Privacy scrubber and opt-out config, [x] Runbook template renderer and example templates, [x] Integration tests and a lightweight load test. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is off; enable via incident-bot config flag snapshot_stream.enabled=true or per-team opt-in. Migration notes: adds a new database table snapshots.metadata (schema migration included) and a small bounded Redis stream for transient payloads. Security review: privacy scrubber reviewed by security (Maria) and no keys are logged. Performance: streamer uses a 128KB ring buffer per active incident and batching to S3/DB exports after TTL to avoid blocking. Testing: unit tests for scrubber and hooks, integration tests that run a simulated incident and assert attachments, and a short canary load test run in perf-lab. Rollout plan: feature flag rollout to internal SRE team for 48h, then enable for a small number of production teams, monitor latency and error counts on incident creation. Related work: integrates with ENG-9485 (runbook templating), SRE-142 (oncall noise reduction) and ENG-9622 (incident exports). How to validate: create an incident via local dev CLI with --snapshot-stream and check /api/v1/incidents/{id}/snapshot, verify Slack message contains expected safe suggestions, and confirm scrubber removes sample PII. Risks & mitigations: potential overcollection mitigated by size caps, privacy risk mitigated by scrubber + opt-out, downstream spam mitigated by rate limits and backoff. Implementation notes: adapters are in internal/escalation/adapters so adding a new provider is a single file implementing the Adapter interface. Docs: added runbooks/escalation-hooks.md and configuration examples. Merge: squash and merge after ci passes and final approval.

review_comments: Connor Blake: Can we bound memory usage per active incident? Suggest 128KB ring buffer by default — addressed in ringbuffer.go and documented in configs/defaults.yaml.
María Fernandez: Verify scrubber patterns cover base64 tokens and common email obfuscations — added tests and updated scrub rules; follow-up to iterate on false positives.
Evan Liu: Slight preference for making Slack adapter async to avoid blocking on network errors — adapters use a buffered worker and exponential backoff now.
Asha Patel (author): Responding to Connor/María/Evan: implemented memory cap, extended scrubber test coverage, made adapters async; added integration tests that simulate transient PD failures.
release_notes: Added incident snapshot stream (opt-in) and cross-team escalation hooks with privacy-scrubbing and runbook templating. Disabled by default; enable via snapshot_stream.enabled flag. Includes Slack and PagerDuty adapters and DB migration for snapshot metadata.
